faq_slots.question: Why does a stain come back after the carpet has been cleaned?
faq_slots.answer_brief: Use the assigned symptom's meaning and its linked local issue. Three genuinely different causes in plain words, from the trade facts what goes wrong rows and the calibration pack: the mark has gone down to the backing or the underlay and rises again as the carpet dries; a shop product's residue left in the pile, drawing dirt to the patch; a hired machine that wets the carpet more than it can suck back. Then what the local factor adds (pets, hard water, tenure), then what a proper clean has to reach. Blame the method, never the customer's effort. Never promise the stain is gone.

faq_slots.answer_brief: Used only when the client's services list carries the end of tenancy page. cards.title: A stain or a mark that came back
cards.brief: Problem led pages (rug, curtain, leather, mattress, pet stain, oven, tile and grout, stone floor, and the exterior pages): the mark that fades and reappears, the smell that stays, the grout that darkens again within weeks, the green that returns on the shaded wall. The one cause this card makes: the cause left underneath, only the surface cleaned (urine through to the backing that wicks back up as the carpet dries, a shop product left in the fibres pulling dirt back in, growth left in the render). From the trade facts what goes wrong rows and the calibration pack: explain what defeated the customer's own go at it, without blaming them, and what a proper clean has to reach. cards.mechanism: the cause left underneath, only the surface cleaned

cards.title: The wrong method for the surface
cards.brief: Every page: the damage a clean does when the method suits the cleaner, not the surface or the room, from the trade facts done badly rows: high pressure on roof tiles, render or block joints; too much water in a carpet; bleach on wool; soap and water on absorbent leather; oven cleaner on a catalytic lining; the same cloth or mop carried from the washroom to the desk or the worktop (the commercial and clinic version of this card, and every home that has both a kitchen and bathrooms). The one cause this card makes: a method chosen for speed, not for the surface. Give the usual principle (a test patch first, cloths and mops colour coded by area, a treatment after the dirt is off, not instead of it) as general practice, never as this client's process unless a tick or a practice confirms it. Never a pressure, a temperature or a dwell time: the rows give none that apply to every surface.
